---
title: "exploring CP plot data"
output: html_document
---
```{r}
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```



```{r}
CP_plots <- read.csv(here("species list data", "CP plots.csv"))

sum(CP_plots$relative_abundance_percent)
```

```{r}
#now I need to correct the names of this dataset
#read in the 'final species list corrected and cleaned'
species_list <- read.csv(here("species list data", "final species list corrected and cleaned.csv"))

#create a new column with corrected binomial name of each species
species_list$binomial_name <- paste(species_list$genus, species_list$species)

species_list <- species_list %>%
  select(original_binomial_name, binomial_name, family, genus, species)

#now to correct the error from creating the final species list, I need to merge species_list and final_species_list 
CP_plots_clean <- full_join(species_list, CP_plots, by = c("original_binomial_name" = "binomial_name")) %>%
  select(binomial_name, family, genus, species, restoration, count, relative_abundance_percent, mean_DBH, mean_Height) %>%
  filter(!is.na(relative_abundance_percent))

#check that all of the relative abundances add up to 200
sum(CP_plots_clean$relative_abundance_percent, na.rm = TRUE)
#yes they do - all good!
```
```{r}
# Step 1: Get top 10 families by total species count (across AR + NR)
top_families <- CP_plots_clean %>%
  group_by(family) %>%
  summarise(total_count = sum(count, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(desc(total_count)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10) %>%
  pull(family)

#collapse other families into 'other'
CP_plots_top_families <- CP_plots_clean %>%
  mutate(family_grouped = ifelse(family %in% top_families, family, "Other"))

#summarise relative abundance per family_grouped and restoration type
summary_data <- CP_plots_top_families %>%
  group_by(restoration, family_grouped) %>%
  summarise(total_abundance = sum(relative_abundance_percent, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

#plot the data
ggplot(summary_data, aes(x = restoration, y = total_abundance, fill = family_grouped)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "turbo") +
  labs(
    x = "Restoration Type",
    y = "Relative Abundance (%)",
    fill = "Family",
    title = ""
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5))
```





```{r}
#now I want to plot the actual number of species in the two sites, from the top 10 families
summary_data_counts <- CP_plots_top_families %>%
  group_by(restoration, family_grouped) %>%
  summarise(total_species_count = sum(count, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(summary_data_counts, aes(x = restoration, y = total_species_count, fill = family_grouped)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "turbo") +
  labs(
    x = "Restoration Type",
    y = "Number of species",
    fill = "Family",
    title = ""
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5))

```
```{r}
#read in the raw TRY data
TRY_data_raw <- read.delim(here("raw trait data", "TRy", "TRY data.txt"))
```

```{r}
#I want to create a separate dataset for each trait, so that the data is easier to handle
# List of TraitIDs you want to filter
trait_ids <- c(207, 28, 26, 239, 919, 917, 4, 3684, 335)

# Create a list to store each subset as a separate data frame
separated_datasets <- list()

# Loop through each TraitID and filter the dataset
for (trait_id in trait_ids) {
  dataset_name <- paste0("TraitID_", trait_id)
  separated_datasets[[dataset_name]] <- TRY_data_raw %>%
    filter(TraitID == trait_id)
}

#create an object for each trait dataset

flower_colour_TRY <- separated_datasets$TraitID_207
#14 records on flower colour, worth working with 

seed_dispersal_syndrome_TRY <- separated_datasets$TraitID_28
#321 entries, worth working with 

seed_dry_mass_TRY <- separated_datasets$TraitID_26
#656 records, worth working with 

seed_width_TRY <- separated_datasets$TraitID_239
#1 records - discard

fruit_dry_mass_TRY <- separated_datasets$TraitID_919
#only 4 different species - not really worth it

fruit_width_TRY <- separated_datasets$TraitID_917
#1 record - discard

wood_density_TRY <- separated_datasets$TraitID_4
#1581 records, worth working with 

crown_elevation_TRY <- separated_datasets$TraitID_3684
#0 records, discard

reproductive_phenology_TRY <- separated_datasets$TraitID_335
#only 5 different species
```

```{r}
#Take seed_dry_mass_TRY and tidy it up:
#select just the columns I want
#rename some columns
#take the mean of each seed mass for each species
#remember this is 1000 seed mass
seed_dry_mass_TRY_clean <- seed_dry_mass_TRY %>%
  select(AccSpeciesName, TraitName, StdValue, UnitName, Reference) %>%
  rename(dry_seed_mass = StdValue, binomial_name = AccSpeciesName) %>%
  group_by(binomial_name) %>%
  summarise(mean_dry_seed_mass_TRY = round(mean(dry_seed_mass, na.rm = TRUE), 2))
```



```{r}
#explore average seed mass
CP_species_list <- CP_plots_clean$binomial_name

CP_species_list <- CP_species_list %>%
  unique()

average_seed_mass_BIEN = BIEN_trait_mean(species = CP_species_list, trait = "seed mass")



```

```{r}
#THIS NEEDS A LOT OF THINKING ABOUT...
#merge species_list and seed_dry_mass_TRY_clean
merged_seed_mass <- left_join(CP_plots_clean, seed_dry_mass_TRY_clean, by = c("binomial_name" = "binomial_name"))%>%
  select(binomial_name, family, genus, species, restoration, count, relative_abundance_percent, mean_DBH, mean_Height, mean_dry_seed_mass_TRY)

#add in BIEN traits
final_seed_mass <- merged_seed_mass %>%
  left_join(average_seed_mass_BIEN, by = c("binomial_name" = "species"))  %>%
  mutate(mean_dry_seed_mass = ifelse(
      is.na(mean_dry_seed_mass_TRY), mean_dry_seed_mass_BIEN, mean_dry_seed_mass_TRY)) %>%
  mutate(mean_dry_seed_mass = as.numeric(mean_dry_seed_mass),
    mean_dry_seed_mass_BIEN = as.numeric(mean_dry_seed_mass_BIEN)) %>%
  select(binomial_name, family, genus, species, restoration, count, relative_abundance_percent, mean_DBH, mean_Height, mean_dry_seed_mass, level_used) %>%
  group_by(binomial_name, restoration) %>%
  summarise(
    seed_mass_CWM = weighted.mean(mean_dry_seed_mass, count), #should I use count or relative abundance to weight the mean?? idk...
    mean_height_CWM = weighted.mean(mean_Height, count),
    mean_DBH_CWM = weighted.mean(mean_DBH, count)
  )
  #mutate(CWM_seed_mass = mean_dry_seed_mass * relative_abundance_percent)

ggplot(final_seed_mass, aes(x = restoration, y = seed_mass_CWM)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, height = 0, alpha = 0.6, color = "blue") +
  labs(
    title = " CWM seed mass",
    x = "restoration status",
    y = " CWM 1000 dry seed mass") +
  theme_minimal()

```
